config._v3_summary: Each evaluation query is measured ONCE, when the workload first serves it; a window strategy repairs that query's missing window documents inline and is charged for them; completion is an admissibility CONSTRAINT, not part of the cost (at completion every strategy has encoded exactly N documents, so cost cannot separate them - what separates them is the quality lost during the migration, 'debt'). See DESIGN.md 'Replay protocol v3'.
config._secondary_under_v3: TREC-DL is evaluation-only, so its queries are never served and have no arrival values; the secondary metric is reported from the fully migrated state (result['final_state']) only.
config._eps_sensitivity: eps decides, on its own, whether a window strategy is admissible at a given depth: it reaches the target iff G(K') <= eps. P4's dev G was 0.013, so at eps=0.01 every window strategy is inadmissible there and S0 wins by default - a winner set by a knob. 'debt' does not depend on eps; the C_serve diagnostic does, and its winner is reported at each of these values.
config._band_tiebreak: How a tie inside the tau band is broken: 'cost' (cheapest by C_serve, then simplicity) or 'simplicity' (the original v3 rule). PRE-REGISTERED. 'cost' is set here because of what the 2026-11-01 1M run showed: every window strategy had debt within 0.0006 of zero, so 12-16 of the 22 combinations sat inside tau = 0.005 and simplicity picked S2/rand on 20 of 21 settings - while inside that same band S2/demand_then_rand reached full population service at 0.835-0.879 of N against S2/rand's 1.000, matching coverage to four decimals. The band therefore contained the entire measured 12-16% saving and the rule discarded it. C_serve is already a pre-registered secondary objective, so ordering the band by it is a stated-ordering change, not a new metric. The function default stays 'simplicity' so an earlier result re-runs to its own winner from its own stored config.
config._tau: Equivalence bands, in each objective's own units. Everything within the band of the best is equivalent and the SIMPLEST of those wins. Without a band a difference far below the noise floor decides a winner: in the v2 dev runs 0.13% of N flipped a pair between S0 and S5. DECIDE both values; 0.005 recall is roughly the dev bootstrap spread at n_eval ~ 3.5k, and 0.02 N is the original proposal.
config._arrival: Under v3 the stream is drawn from the whole servable workload, so repeat_rate is not used: the mix of evaluation and other queries is the workload's own, not a knob. A setting that cannot serve min_eval_served of its evaluation population inside max_rounds reports NO winner rather than a misleading one. Both min_eval_served and arrival_target_frac are shares of the WORKLOAD WEIGHT, not of the query count, because every quality number is workload-weighted. Under a skewed workload the two differ by orders of magnitude: at a 35,000x weight spread, 99% of the weight is served by round ~100 while 99% of the count takes ~30,000 rounds, since the tail is almost never drawn. Gating on the count would reject every ORCAS and Zipf setting. The count is reported alongside as a diagnostic.
config._traffic_ratio: traffic_ratio = (queries served per round x window) / background encodings per round. It is the one parameter that decides whether reuse can pay at all, because cost-to-serve has a floor at the background work already done by the last arrival.
config._max_rounds_factor: max_rounds = factor x rounds must exceed (arrival rounds) + rounds, or 'demand_then_rand' cannot complete and the run is reported as an ARRIVAL SHORTFALL. 8 covers ratio >= 4 at these sizes; scripts/predict.py prints the requirement per ratio.
config._orders: 'demand_then_rand' holds background work back until every evaluation query has arrived, then completes: under the v3 objective it is the cost-minimal policy that still completes, so leaving it out would mean the best admissible policy is not in the search space. 'demand' never completes and is reported separately, never as a winner (it is also the policy whose economics are Thaw's C2, out of scope here).
config._mode: first_service requires sync: an arriving query must have its window repaired inline to be servable at target quality. The runner refuses any other mode.
config._preregistered: 2026-11-06 on bjb1, before any v3 pair ran in this round. Values are unchanged from the draft: eval_frac 0.5, traffic grid [4,16,64,256], primary traffic_ratio 64 (placeholder for ORCAS, stated as such), delta 0.01, eps 0.01 (+sensitivity 0.005/0.01/0.02), tau debt 0.005 / c_serve 0.02, band_tiebreak cost, probe 12 x 250 (code 8 x 100). window_frac stays the placeholder on purpose: RUNBOOK Phase 1 makes it a two-stage decision settled from the 5.5 frontier.

_window_decided.rule: smallest K' with G<=eps on every pair (RUNBOOK 5.5e / 11.1)
_window_decided.outcome: 10 is admissible only for P5 and P14; 25 is admissible for nine pairs but P11 sits at 0.01368 > eps, so 50 is the smallest depth that works everywhere. The ceiling is therefore 73.5%, not the 85-90% that K'=10/25 would give.
_window_decided.reproducibility: the whole 10/25/50 frontier matches the 2026-11-04 run digit for digit, on freshly re-encoded vectors (5 models re-encoded under contracts, 5x23 encode_check passed, 0 failure)

config._preregistered_scale: The static scale study was pre-registered 2026-11-10, before any full-corpus (8.8M) vector existed. The scale configs hold the query population fixed and use a 50-document window rather than window_frac x N so corpus sizes are compared at the same depth. Those original static predictions remain in PREREG_SCALE.md. Final2 adds a separate replay test at fixed K'=50; this metadata note does not change any numeric parameter.
config._replay_trim: Replay at 8.8M: as msmarco_s2m_v3_replay.json, on the full corpus.
config._kprime: The ladder the replay measures rho and G on: 25, 50, 100 (the K'-fraction ladder of the 1M config reaches 44,209 at 8.8M and only costs time).

notes: I6 evaluation queries are measured at first service only, never re-scored after their own repair: ok (enforced in run_arrivals)
